subject: Economics
description: Govt revenue + spending; deficit; FRBM; direct vs indirect tax

questions.stem: FISCAL POLICY refers to government use of:

options.option_text: Interest rates set by the central bank
Taxation + expenditure to influence economy
Foreign exchange reserves only as tool
Currency devaluation as the chief policy

questions.explanation: FISCAL policy = Government's use of TAXATION + SPENDING to influence economy. Set by Finance Ministry / Govt. Tools: tax rates, subsidy, public spending, borrowing. EXPANSIONARY (boost growth): cut taxes, raise spending → stimulates demand, but raises deficit. CONTRACTIONARY (curb inflation): raise taxes, cut spending. Distractor 1 = MONETARY policy (RBI). Distractor 4 = exchange rate policy. Both fiscal + monetary policies are macroeconomic levers; ideally coordinated.
questions.subject: Economics

options.option_text: Revenue receipts minus revenue expenditure (revenue gap)
Total expenditure minus total receipts (excluding borrowing)
Capital receipts minus capital expenditure (capital gap)
Tax revenue minus subsidy spending of govt budget

questions.explanation: FISCAL DEFICIT = Total Expenditure − Total Receipts (EXCLUDING BORROWINGS). i.e., the GAP that government fills by borrowing. India's FD target (FRBM) was 3% of GDP; suspended during pandemic; FY24 ~5.6%, glide path to 4.5% by FY26. Other deficits: REVENUE DEFICIT = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts (= 'living beyond means'); PRIMARY DEFICIT = FD − interest payments (true gap excluding past-debt servicing); EFFECTIVE REVENUE DEFICIT = RD − grants for capital creation. FD financed by: market borrowing (G-secs), small savings, foreign loans, RBI ways-and-means.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a DIRECT TAX in India?

options.option_text: GST on goods + services bought
Income tax (paid directly by taxpayer)
Customs duty on imports + exports
Excise duty on alcohol or fuel

questions.explanation: DIRECT TAX = paid DIRECTLY by the person on whom it's levied; cannot be shifted. Examples: INCOME TAX (individuals + companies), CORPORATE TAX, CAPITAL GAINS TAX. Govt body: CBDT (Central Board of Direct Taxes). INDIRECT TAX = levied on goods/services; can be shifted to consumers (built into price). Examples: GST (replaced excise, service tax, VAT, etc., from July 2017), CUSTOMS DUTY (on imports — and few exports), STAMP DUTY (state-level). Govt body: CBIC (Central Board of Indirect Taxes + Customs). Indian taxes: ~50% direct + ~50% indirect (varies year to year).

questions.stem: FRBM Act (Fiscal Responsibility + Budget Management Act, 2003) was enacted to:

options.option_text: Increase government borrowing limits in budget
Reduce + control fiscal deficit progressively
Increase tax rates substantially every year
Privatize all public sector banks (PSBs)

questions.explanation: FRBM ACT, 2003 — enacted to bring fiscal discipline. Targets: (1) eliminate revenue deficit by FY09 (postponed); (2) reduce fiscal deficit to 3% of GDP. RBI ways-and-means lending to govt phased out by 2006. RBI cannot subscribe to PRIMARY auction of govt bonds (must buy in secondary market). Original targets often missed + RELAXED. Pandemic 2020 → suspended. Current glide path: FD to 4.5% of GDP by FY26 (FY24 actual ~5.6%). Critics argue FRBM is too rigid; defenders say discipline avoids crowding out + fiscal crisis. NK SINGH committee (2017) recommended 'debt rule' framework (debt-to-GDP target).

questions.stem: GST (Goods and Services Tax) rolled out in India on:

options.option_text: 26 January 2015 (Republic Day)
1 July 2017 (midnight launch)
15 August 2018 (Independence Day)
1 April 2020 (start of FY)

questions.explanation: GST launched at MIDNIGHT 1 JULY 2017 — special joint session of Parliament. Replaced ~17 indirect taxes (excise, service tax, VAT, OCTROI, entertainment, luxury, central sales tax). 'ONE NATION, ONE TAX'. 4 main rate slabs: 5%, 12%, 18%, 28% (+ 0% essentials, special 0.25% gold, special 3% gold). GST COUNCIL (chair: Finance Minister; 1 minister per state) decides rates. INPUT TAX CREDIT — businesses claim back tax paid on inputs. CGST + SGST + IGST (interstate). 101st Amendment Act (2016) enabled GST. Implementation initially rocky (multiple slabs, compliance burden) — gradually streamlined. Approved by every state + UT.

questions.stem: REVENUE RECEIPTS of the central government primarily come from:

options.option_text: Sale of public sector enterprises in budget
Tax revenue + non-tax revenue (interest etc.)
Borrowing from Reserve Bank of India only
Foreign aid + grants from foreign countries

questions.explanation: REVENUE RECEIPTS = TAX REVENUE (income tax, GST, customs, corporation, excise) + NON-TAX REVENUE (interest on loans, dividends from PSUs, fees, fines, RBI surplus, spectrum auction in part). CAPITAL RECEIPTS = borrowing (mostly market loans), disinvestment (sale of stake in PSUs), recoveries of loans. NOT a 'receipt' but financing: RBI ways-and-means / OD. Distractor 1 = capital (disinvestment). Distractor 3 = capital. Distractor 4 = small fraction.

questions.stem: The annual UNION BUDGET in India is presented by:

options.option_text: Prime Minister of India in Parliament
Finance Minister of Govt of India
RBI Governor from the Mumbai office
Niti Aayog Chairman in the Parliament

questions.explanation: UNION BUDGET = Annual Financial Statement (Article 112). Presented by FINANCE MINISTER in Lok Sabha, traditionally on the LAST WORKING DAY OF FEBRUARY at 5 PM, but from FY18 shifted to 1 FEBRUARY at 11 AM (allows Parliament to pass before April 1 fiscal year start). RAILWAY BUDGET (separate since 1924) merged with UNION BUDGET from 2017. Indira GANDHI (1969) — only PM to present budget (held FM portfolio briefly). MORARJI DESAI presented MOST budgets (10). NIRMALA SITHARAMAN (since 2019) — first full-time woman FM (Indira had been acting FM); has presented 6 budgets (FY 20-25). Special: 'KAR LAGE BAHI' (a tradition the PM once thanked her for, ditched in 2019).
